name: Gloaming

synthesis.essence: The last light is a reading, not a mood.
synthesis.oneSentence: A rangeland stewardship cooperative's field instrument, built from one blue-hour plate: a pane of optical glass laid across the horizon, with everything that must be read printed solid underneath it.
synthesis.promise: Gloaming turns one hour of low light over a working meadow into a record a land steward can check: ridge, oak, lupine, herd, horizon. The pane refracts the sky; the plate holds the numbers.
synthesis.material: one hazy blue-hour plate + a 26px refracting pane + solid oat reading plates
synthesis.edge: 22px squircle, 1px inset rim, 1px mullions, one lit top edge
synthesis.mechanism: A horizon cut through one pane of optical glass: above the cut the last light refracts, below it the land prints solid, and the cut itself is the 4-unit bar of the mark.
synthesis.hero: A · banner, then a number row · relation below
synthesis.styleReason: Q1 was an explicit named pick of #19 Liquid glass. The supplied plate is a photograph-like hazy gradient with a hard warm horizon, which is exactly the single ground #19 calls for. Mullion (22) already owns urban glass massing and Wildflower Wind (13) owns a frosted seed-house meadow, so this case takes the glass to a working landscape and keeps the accent apricot, not red or violet.

mark.geometry: A 4-unit horizon bar at y46-50 carrying two hill panes split by a 4-unit mullion at x29-33. The right crest sits 4 units higher than the left: that step is the refraction, and it is the one ownable cut carried into the wordmark.
